newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power mixed ahead of cold weekend - 8/11.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power mixed ahead of cold weekend - 8/11.

text.p: Wholesale physical electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished mixed on Friday amid forecasts for sharply lower temperatures this weekend, traders said.
"We haven't seen much change in prices," said one New York trader. "The load isn't really going be high this weekend. We won't see big changes in temperatures until early next week."
But according to Weather Services Corp, much colder air would arrive late Saturday into Sunday lasting until Tuesday with temperatures 12 to 17 Fahrenheit below seasonal norms.
The 610 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point unit 1 in Scriba, N.Y., was expected to resume service over the weekend after tripping off line Tuesday because of a generator problem.

In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Saturday delivery was quoted near $17.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), for Sunday at $16.50-$16.75 and for Monday at $22.00-$23.00. Today's quotes compared with Thursday's $22.00-$23.00 for Friday delivery.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Friday remained at $13.50-$14.50.
With expected modest weekend load, some Northeast utilities planned to put their more expensive oil and natural gas-fired generating units into so-called reserve shutdown, marketers and traders said.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for this weekend was near $20.00 and for Monday $26.00-$27.00. Those values compared with Thursday's $30.00-$31.00 for Friday delivery.
Off-peak, non-firm Friday electricity in eastern NYPP held steady at $16.00-$18.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted again at $34.00-$35.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was notationally pegged at $21.00-$22.00, flat from Thursday.

The New York Power Authority planned to restore a 765 kilovolt (KV) transmission power line from Quebec to New York to normal operation after shutting two segments of the line last weekend for seasonal maintenance.
